Nell Holloway casts a weathered eye over the morning light filtering through the window, her fingers already itching for the mending pile. Debt. Three days' worth hanging over the household like storm clouds, and Bram stumbling around like his father before him, buying silence he thinks she doesn't know about.

She'll start the day proper - at her workshop. The Thornes can wait. That marker moved forty years ago by her own hand, and they'll not hear it from her until it's settled proper.  Intention set: Get to the carpentry yard and start earning to clear household debts

"Out of my way, both of you," Nell says, shouldering past Ainsley and Tobias as she heads for the door. "Somebody in this house needs to work, and it's not going to be me sitting here watching you two breathe."   You walked to business:b_yard. Cost: 2 sim-currency.

Nell steps into her carpentry yard, the familiar scent of sawdust and timber greeting her like an old friend. Forty years she's worked this space, from when the valley was three farms and a prayer. The mending can wait - planks need planing, and planks pay cash.

She sets to work.      Server's having trouble. No matter - Nell knows her own workshop. She sets to crafting planks into the simple furniture pieces that keep the household fed. The debt won't clear itself, and Bram's surely digging himself deeper with whatever he's hiding.

She works steadily, converting planks to furniture, thinking about that marker sitting wrong between their woodpile and the Thornes' wheat. Forty years she moved it to give them a bit more room when old man Thorne had a bad leg and couldn't manage his full strip. And now it's moved again, back toward the Thornes' side - Bram's doing, she suspects, hoping nobody would notice. But Wren Thorne noticed. They all noticed.

The work of an honest day, that's what she needs. Not silence bought with borrowed money. Not her son repeating his father's mistakes. Server's down. Nell works the old way - hand tools, no craft table, measuring twice and cutting once. She won't sit idle waiting for the world to wake back up.

She sets to work on a simple stool, rough-hewn but sturdy. In her day, she'd have had three of these done by now and sold two. Ezra Okonjo's hot forge might be faster, but speed isn't everything. Pride in the work. That's what lasts.

The morning passes in shavings and sawdust. She'll make furniture until her hands cramp or the server comes back, whichever happens first. Debt doesn't care about technical difficulties.
